Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.

Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.

- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.

Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The Sunrise Bakery entry interrupts the quantitative trajectory and is positioned too prominently.
items.because: It puts unrelated retail operations ahead of evidence more relevant to a quantitative research role.

items.says: Quant-focused experience and projects should appear before education.
The weekly labour-budget result has no measure.
items.because: The reader cannot judge how close to or consistently within budget the store operated.

items.says: The 35% improvement does not identify its measure or comparison.
items.because: Without a metric and baseline, the result is difficult to interpret.

items.says: The signal-smoothing achievement overlaps with the later Northpeak signal bullet.
items.because: The reader may interpret the two bullets as duplicate claims rather than separate contributions.

items.says: The validation procedure does not ensure every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: Purging and embargoing do not by themselves control feature timestamps, data revisions, vendor availability, or future-derived preprocessing.

items.says: The validation line gives no result.
items.because: Six years of tick data shows the test's scale, not whether the signal survived it or what decision it supported.

items.says: The feature store's adoption result is buried in a relative clause.
The capacity estimate and live allocation are not measurable.
The deployment result is buried behind vague wording.
The best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations is invalid as an expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the maximum introduces selection bias, and the same backtests cannot provide an unbiased live-performance estimate without an independent holdout or adjustment.

items.says: The strongest result is delayed by a long method description.
Using the same random seed on every worker may duplicate random-number streams and invalidate the 2,000-run count.
items.because: Identical seeds ordinarily produce identical sequences rather than independent Monte Carlo replicates.

items.says: The parallelization framework and worker assignment are not identified.
The log-factor improvement does not specify the old and new bound forms.
“My proof” breaks résumé-bullet style.
The package's user value is unclear.
items.because: Downloads show exposure, not whether users adopted the methods or gained a capability.

items.says: The writer's implementation ownership is unclear.
items.because: “Released” does not establish whether they authored the package and implemented its methods.

items.says: The past-tense opening is inconsistent with the study's current status.
The crisis-period scope is unclear.
The result is stated less directly than statistical significance.
The line gives no concrete consequence of the study or presentation.
The description of the analytical work is generic.
The feature-engineering and modeling activity has no stated competition result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the models performed well or what the team contributed to the outcome.

items.says: The closing phrase repeats the competition context in the heading.
items.because: It uses space without adding evidence.

items.says: The 0.02 gap lacks a metric and before-and-after values.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what 0.02 represents or how substantial the change was.

items.says: The gap reduction is buried after the method.
items.because: Leading with the reduction would make the result easier to scan.

items.says: The 0.4 Sharpe increase lacks a comparison point.
items.because: Without a baseline or prior value, the reader cannot judge the starting level or resulting performance.

items.says: The validation wording makes the out-of-sample scope harder to scan.
The bullet repeats the Northpeak order-book signal and 18-month result without distinguishing the project.
items.because: The matching signal, period, and implied 0.4 Sharpe change leave it unclear which project produced the result.

items.says: Kafka is listed under Programming without supporting evidence elsewhere in the résumé.
“econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: A spelling error in a Methods skill makes the section look insufficiently proofread.
